transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm here because I've been struggling with really intense delusions and paranoia, and sometimes I even hear voices that aren't there. At the same time, I've been dealing with severe mood swings where I feel extremely energetic and high. This has all been going on for about two years now, and it's getting very hard to manage.
Have you ever experienced the voices or paranoia during times when your mood felt completely normal and stable, or do they only happen when you are feeling very high and energetic?

Yes, I've definitely experienced them when my mood was completely normal. There was a period of about two or three weeks where I felt totally stable and calm, but I still heard the voices and felt paranoid. It doesn't just happen when I'm feeling high or energetic.
Looking back over the past two years, would you say these periods of extreme highs—or any periods of deep depression—have been present for most of that time, or are they relatively brief?

Yes, over the past two years, those periods of extreme highs have definitely been present for the majority of the time. Any times where I felt really depressed or low have been much briefer in comparison.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports experiencing delusions and auditory hallucinations for a period of 2-3 weeks in the absence of any mood symptoms, which rules out Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features (where psychosis only occurs during a mood episode). Additionally, the patient states that the manic episodes (extreme highs) have been present for the majority of the two-year illness duration, which meets Criterion C for Schizoaffective Disorder and rules out Schizophrenia (where mood episodes are relatively brief). Therefore, the diagnosis is Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type).
